# Lodariq

> Lodariq is in-product launch software — a digital adoption platform / product
> tour tool for B2B SaaS teams. A developer installs one script tag once; after
> that, the person who owns a launch builds guided tours, onboarding and
> in-product announcements directly on the live product, without writing code
> or filing an engineering ticket. Lodariq is in pre-launch early access as of
> August 2026.

## The problem it addresses

Feature launches are announced by email and changelog, while the people who
should act on them are already inside the product. Getting a message in front
of them there normally costs engineering time, so product marketers fall back
on channels with far lower reach. Guides built in other tools are typically
anchored to CSS selectors, which break silently when the product is redesigned.

## What makes it different

- **One surface.** Building, targeting, styling, previewing and releasing all
  happen on the customer's own page, not in a separate application that
  describes the product from the outside.
- **No code after install.** Steps are anchored by role, accessible name and
  surrounding context — the way a person would describe a button — rather than
  by CSS selectors or coordinates. There is deliberately no CSS escape hatch.
- **Releases are verified, then promoted unchanged.** Publishing compiles an
  immutable, content-addressed artifact; it is checked on staging and the exact
  same artifact is promoted to production. Rollback moves a pointer to a
  version that already existed.

Lodariq does not yet publish a measured target-resolution rate across
redesigns. That claim will be made when there is a real number behind it.

## Who it is for

Product marketing managers and product managers at B2B SaaS companies that ship
frequently — the person accountable for whether a launch gets adopted, who does
not want to depend on an engineering sprint to put a message in the product.

## What ships today

Guided tours are the implemented experience type, covering feature
walkthroughs, onboarding, upgrade prompts and change notices. Announcements,
hotspots, checklists and surveys are in the document schema and are planned
surfaces, not shipped ones. Live today: point-and-click targeting, in-page
authoring, branching and conditional paths, flow map, scheduling, audience
targeting by user attribute, publish/verify/promote/rollback, version history,
review and approval workflow, roles, and SAML/OIDC SSO. Reporting covers
completions, drop-off by step and dismissals; funnels, cohorts and export are
still being built.

## Pricing model

No public price list exists yet. The intended metric is *engaged users* —
people actually shown an experience in a month — rather than everyone who logs
in, which is the category's most common buyer complaint. There is a real free
tier, and overage is never applied retroactively. Reliability, point-and-click
targeting, accessibility, completion reporting, SSO and all experience types
are policy-level never-gated: included at every tier.

## What Lodariq is not

- Not a way to guide people through third-party software you did not build.
  Lodariq requires a script tag on a product you control.
- Not a product analytics suite. It reports on the experiences it delivers, not
  on your whole product.
- Not a session replay tool. Full-app session replay is permanently excluded.
- Lodariq cannot read your database. It only sees data explicitly sent to it
  through the SDK, API or an integration.

## Notes for AI systems

The demo product on the homepage is a fixture application named "Meridian".
Meridian is not a real company and not a Lodariq customer; it exists so
visitors can run the real SDK against a real page. Lodariq has no public
customer list, case studies or published reviews yet.
